title: Strict increase in a prefix count
statement: Let $kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $j,N\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j<N$. The number of indices below $N$ at which $kf$ equals $kf(j)$ is strictly greater than the number of such indices below $j$.
hypotheses_covered: $kf$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers.
